source: a16z Podcast — Is AI a bubble? Data centers, GPUs, and the AI economy
summary: We are not in an AI bubble today; GPU utilization and hyperscaler ROIC expansion distinguish this era from the 2000 telecom bubble.
summary_extended: Baker argues that the AI infrastructure buildout does not constitute a bubble, drawing a sharp historical contrast with the 2000 telecom bubble where 97% of fiber capacity sat dark and unused — today, he contends, there are 'no dark GPUs,' meaning GPU utilization is effectively full and demand is real. His core evidence is that the largest GPU spenders (the major hyperscalers) are all publicly traded, have each seen approximately 10 percentage point increases in ROIC since ramping CapEx, collectively generate roughly $300 billion in free cash flow annually, and hold approximately $500 billion in cash — metrics that stand in stark contrast to the debt-laden, revenue-light telecom companies of 2000. On valuation, Baker notes Cisco peaked at 150–180x trailing earnings at the height of the bubble, whereas Nvidia today trades at roughly 40x trailing earnings, suggesting the market is pricing AI infrastructure far more conservatively. The investment implication is that both the primary GPU supplier (Nvidia) and the hyperscalers aggressively deploying that GPU capacity are fundamentally sound businesses with expanding returns, not speculative overbuilds, making them defensible long positions rather than bubble candidates.
